blocks.text: Particular note should be taken of what pertains to the description. Thus Avicenna, book 5, p. 179, in the chapter entitled صنعة اقراص الافاعي [ṣanʿat aqrāṣ al-afāʿī] The art of the troches of alaphai, that is, of vipers, says: الافاعي هي الحياة المفرطحة الرووس المستعرضتها خصوصا عند قرب الرقبة الدقاق رقابها جدا البتر اذنابها الفحاحة الكشاشة وليس يصلح لهذا الاقراص كل الافاعي بل الشقر ومن الشقر الاناث وعلامتها ان الذكر [col. 361] في كل شدق ناب واحد وللاناث اكثر من ناب واحد [al-afāʿī hiya al-ḥayyāt al-mufarṭaḥat al-ruʾūs al-mustaʿriḍatuhā khuṣūṣan ʿinda qurb al-raqaba al-diqāq riqābuhā jiddan al-butr adhnābuhā al-faḥḥāḥat al-kashshāsha wa-laysa yaṣluḥu li-hādhā al-aqrāṣ kull al-afāʿī bal al-shuqr wa-min al-shuqr al-ināth wa-ʿalāmatuhā anna al-dhakar fī kull shidq nāb wāḥid wa-li-l-ināth akthar min nāb wāḥid] Alaphai (vipers) are serpents with flat heads, very broad especially around the neck, with a very slender neck, a truncated tail, a clear hiss, and a noisy gait. Yet not all الافاعي [al-afāʿī] alaphai (vipers) are good for these troches, but the red ones, and of the red ones the females. Their mark is that, whereas the male has one canine tooth on each side of the jaw, the female has several ^{(2)}. Hence the same author, book 4, in the chapter في [III, 129] لسع الافاعي [fī lasʿ al-afāʿī] On the bite of alaphai (vipers), Arab. p. 137, Lat. Fen 6, tract. 3, ch. 32: لسع الانثي تعرف بوجود مغارز لاكثر من نابين في الجهة التي عض بها [lasʿ al-unthā tuʿrafu bi-wujūd maghāriz li-akthar min nābayn fī al-jiha allatī ʿaḍḍa bihā] The bite of the female is recognized from the fact that more than two canine teeth are found to have been driven into the part which it attacked with its bite. Everyone can see that this belongs to the description of the viper, about which Aelian, book 10 of the Hist., ch. 9, says: Νίκανδρος δέ φησιν, ἐκ μὲν τοῦ δήγματος, ὅπερ οὖν ὁ ἔχις ἐμφύει, δύο ὀδόντων ἴχνη φαίνεσθαι· πλέον δὲ, εἰ δάκοι ἡ ἔχιδνα. [Nikandros de phēsin, ek men tou dēgmatos, hoper oun ho echis emphyei, dyo odontōn ichnē phainesthai; pleon de, ei dakoi hē echidna.] Nicander says that from the bite which the echis (that is, the male viper) inflicts, the marks of two teeth appear; but more when the echidna bites, that is, the female viper: which is to be understood of the canines. For so Nicander in the Theriaca, verse 231:
Τοῦ μὲν ὑπὲρ κυνόδοντε δύο χροῒ τεκμαίρονται Ἰὸν ἐρευγόμενοι· πλέονες δέ τοι αἰὲν ἐχίδνης· [Tou men hyper kynodonte dyo chroi tekmairontai / Ion ereugomenoi; pleones de toi aien echidnēs;]

Him (the echis) two canine teeth (impressed) in the body betray, belching out poison; but the echidna (that is, the female viper) always more. And Galen, book 2, On Theriac, ch. 13: Τούτῳ γὰρ τοῦ ἄῤῥενος ἡ ἔχιδνα διήνεγκε τῷ πλέονας τῶν δύο κυνοδόντων ἔχειν· [Toutō gar tou arrhenos hē echidna diēnenke tō pleonas tōn dyo kynodontōn echein;] For in this the female viper differs from the male, that it has more than two canine teeth. Κυνόδους [Kynodous], canine tooth, is in Arabic ناب [nāb], the word which Avicenna uses. Further, on the viper's broad head, slender neck, truncated tail and yellow colour, see Galen and Aëtius; from whom, however, Avicenna differs in that he attributes to vipers in general what they attribute only to the female.

It should moreover be noted that in Abenbitar the whole chapter of Dioscorides On the flesh of the viper is referred to افعى [afʿā] ephe. And these words of his, Ἐχίδνης σὰρξ ἑψηθεῖσα, καὶ ἐσθιομένη, ὀξυδερκεῖς ποιεῖ τὰς ὄψεις [Echidnēs sarx hepsētheisa, kai esthiomenē, oxyderkeis poiei tas opseis], are rendered in Arabic thus: لحم الافاعي اذا طبخ واكل يحد البصر [laḥm al-afāʿī idhā ṭubikha wa-ukila yuḥiddu al-baṣar] The flesh of alaphai, cooked and eaten, sharpens the sight. Again, to these words of the Greek text, Κατασκευάζονται δὲ καὶ ἅλες ἐξ αὐτῶν πρὸς [III, 130] τὰ αὐτὰ, πλὴν οὐχ᾽ ὁμοίως ἐνεργοῦσι [Kataskeuazontai de kai hales ex autōn pros ta auta, plēn ouch homoiōs energousi], correspond these Arabic ones: وقد يعمل ملح من لحوم الافاعي يفعل فعل الافاعي غير انه انقص فعلا منه [wa-qad yuʿmalu milḥ min luḥūm al-afāʿī yafʿalu fiʿl al-afāʿī ghayr annahu anqaṣ fiʿlan minhu] A salt is also made from the flesh of alaphai, which has the same effect as alaphai, except that it is of lesser efficacy. In the same place the Greek reads: Καθίεται δὲ ἔχιδνα ζῶσα εἰς καινὴν χύτραν· [Kathietai de echidna zōsa eis kainēn chytran;] and the Arabic: توخذ افعي حية وتصير في قدر جديدة [tuʾkhadhu afʿā ḥayya wa-tuṣayyaru fī qidr jadīda] An ephe is taken alive and put into a new pot [col. 362]. In the same Abenbitar a lengthy passage of Galen is cited, in which it is shown that lepers are healed by eating viper's flesh. Its beginning is as follows: لحوم الافاعي تجدها عيانا تسخن وتجفف البدن اذا هي طيبت كما يطيب لحم المرماهي بالزيت والملح والشبث والكراث والما بمقدار قصد [luḥūm al-afāʿī tajiduhā ʿiyānan tusakhkhinu wa-tujaffifu al-badan idhā hiya ṭuyyibat kamā yuṭayyabu laḥm al-marmāhī bi-l-zayt wa-l-milḥ wa-l-shibith wa-l-kurrāth wa-l-māʾ bi-miqdār qaṣd] You will plainly find that the flesh of alaphai (vipers) warms and dries the body, when it is seasoned like eels, with oil, salt, dill, leek, and a suitable measure of water. This reads thus in Greek in On Simple Medicines, book 2, ch. 1: Τὰς γοῦν τῶν ἐχιδνῶν θερμαινούσας τε, καὶ ξηραινούσας, ἐναργῶς ἐστιν ἰδεῖν ἀρτυομένας, ὥσπερ αἱ ἐγχέλεις, ἐλαίῳ, καὶ ἁλσὶ, καὶ ἀνήθῳ, καὶ πράσῳ, καὶ ὕδατι, δηλονότι κατὰ τοῦ συμμέτρου. [Tas goun tōn echidnōn thermainousas te, kai xērainousas, enargōs estin idein artyomenas, hōsper hai encheleis, elaiō, kai halsi, kai anēthō, kai prasō, kai hydati, dēlonoti kata tou symmetrou.] See the rest there.

In Alkazuinius it is said of الافعي [al-afʿā] alephe: قد اظلمت عيناها تطلب شجرة الرازيانج وتحك عينها بها يرجع اليها ضوها [qad aẓlamat ʿaynāhā taṭlubu shajarat al-rāziyānaj wa-taḥukku ʿaynahā bihā yarjiʿu ilayhā ḍawʾuhā] When its eyes are blinded, it seeks fennel to rub them with, so as to recover its sight. Indeed, in Andromachus' poem On the composition of pastilles from vipers, these serpents are described, around the beginning of spring,
Διζόμενοι χλωροῦ σπέρμα λαβεῖν μαράθρου, ᾽Οξυτέρην τὸ τίθησιν ἐφ᾽ ἑρπυστῆρσιν ὀπωπήν· [Dizomenoi chlōrou sperma labein marathrou, / Oxyterēn to tithēsin eph' herpystērsin opōpēn;]
